plan.analysis: L1 is stuck at 0.940795: the resolution sweep to 2x N changed nothing, so finer grids alone are not the bottleneck. Two structural limits are visible in p0002's code: the log-parametrised L-BFGS freezes the support (active set = h > 1e-13*max), so the 20.9% zeros can never open and small entries can never vanish; and ||f*f||_inf is handled through a single argmax knot, which forbids flattening the peak plateau (42.8% of knots are within 5% of max). I bet on (1) active-set support moves using the gradient at zero entries, (2) a smoothed soft-max surrogate with temperature annealing so several near-max knots are driven down together, and (3) an independent coarse multi-start from random shapes, prolongated only if better, as a different basin rather than more polishing of the same one.

experiments.hypothesis: The support pattern has never been re-optimised: _lbfgs_log freezes active = h > 1e-13*max, so 20.9% forced zeros are permanent and near-zero spikes cannot die. Making the support a free variable (drop weak entries, admit entries whose gradient at zero is downhill) lets the optimiser reshape the tails, where the R deficit lives.
experiments.change: Add a working-set loop around _lbfgs_log. (a) Compute the full gradient g = _backprop(gLf, h) + 2/s for the current h including at zero entries, i.e. evaluate the gradient of val = -log(num)+2log(s)+log(max) at h with zero positions still zero (do not restrict to the active set). (b) Drop: set to exactly 0 the smallest 1% of positive entries whose removal does not increase val (or simply the 1% smallest h). (c) Admit: among zero positions, pick the 1% with the most negative g_i and set them to 1e-3 * mean(h). (d) Re-run _lbfgs_log with the new active set, keep the result only if R improves. Repeat this add/drop cycle inside the main loop until deadline-1.0 s, then run the existing peak/phase polish on the best. Report 'support: k zeros, R=...' after each cycle.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.9420 on L1 (from 0.940795). Success shows as a decreasing zero-fraction with better R in the support lines; if the zero count returns to ~21% each cycle, the support is already optimal and the plateau is elsewhere.

experiments.hypothesis: ||f*f||_inf is non-smooth; using only argmax(Lf) means the peak is pinned at one knot and nearby knots just under the max are unpenalised. A temperature-annealed soft-max penalises a whole plateau of knots, letting the peak region flatten and raising ||f*f||_2^2 relative to the max.
experiments.change: Add a second optimiser path using the surrogate val_tau = -log(num) + 2 log(s) + tau * logsumexp(Lf / tau), with gradient gLf = -dq/num + softmax(Lf/tau) (derivative of tau*logsumexp), backpropagated as now. Do continuation over tau = 0.02, 0.005, 0.001, 2e-4, 1e-4 times max(Lf), each stage an L-BFGS-B call on log-heights (reuse _lbfgs_log but with this value/gradient), maxiter 300 per stage. After the final stage run 200 more (exact) iterations with the current hard-max objective and take the result only if R beats best. Run this once from the start; if it improves, repeat the anneal from the improved point while time remains.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.9415. The diagnostic is the fraction of knots within 0.1%/1% of max (currently 19.5%/33.9%): success should raise the 0.1% fraction while ||f*f||_inf falls slightly for fixed ||f*f||_2^2; no change means the peak is already a single sharp knot that grading cannot smooth.

experiments.hypothesis: Every experiment so far has polished the same basin; the resolution sweep failing to move anything suggests a local optimum that improvements-of-the-same-kind cannot escape. Independent random shapes at coarse N, optimised and prolongated, probe different basins.
experiments.change: Before any polishing, allocate roughly the first 60% of the budget to a coarse multi-start: N_c = 512. Draw 10 random starts: heights = product of a random envelope (e.g. exp of a random walk with 3-6 random knot amplitudes interpolated over [0,N_c]) times a random sparse mask (each entry zero with probability drawn uniformly in {0.1,0.3,0.5}); ensure sum > 0. Run _lbfgs_log (the full-vector log-height version) with maxiter 400 on each within a per-start time slice; keep the best R_c. Prolongate the best to N = 16384, re-run _lbfgs_log 400 iters; then prolongate to the start resolution 84992 and polish with the existing _window_polish_peak schedule. Return whichever of this and the polished start has higher R.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.942. If none of the 10 coarse starts beats 0.940 after prolongation, that is informative: the shape class is genuinely narrow and future gains must come from support/peak smoothing, not from restarts. Report each coarse start's R so the shape diversity is visible.

plan.analysis: L1 is stuck at 0.940795. Every height-only polish, support working-set, softmax, random multistart, and smoothing experiment returned the start unchanged, so the frozen discrete support and relative placement of spikes are the likely bottleneck. F5 shows multiscale refinement works from a trivial start but is far below this basin. I am betting on changing support combinatorics directly: move/split/merge spikes, displace or rescale one cluster relative to another, and seed new support with a deterministic periodic modulation. Target is a measurable gain above 0.9408; unchanged results would confirm the current support is locally optimal.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002's heights are locally optimal but its nonzero support positions are frozen; F1 only added/removed zero entries by gradient, never moved existing spikes. Translating, splitting, or merging spike components should change the convolution overlap pattern and can escape the height-only local optimum.
experiments.change: Implement a support-move loop. From best, find connected nonzero components (threshold 1e-6*max) and local maxima. Repeat until deadline-2s: copy best; pick one component weighted by mass and either (a) translate it by an integer d in {-16,...,-1,1,...,16}, adding heights where it overlaps and clipping at array ends, (b) split it into two copies separated by d with half mass each, or (c) merge it with the nearest other component. Then run _lbfgs_log on all entries in a window spanning old and new positions plus 10% margin, followed by full _lbfgs_log. Accept only if R_of improves by >1e-9. Keep the best; print each accepted trial.
experiments.prediction: Aims for >=0.9410 on L1. A gain of >=1e-4 shows support combinatorics was limiting; no gain means the current spike positions are locally optimal and a full combinatorial reconstruction is needed.

experiments.hypothesis: The f*f maximum at 0.296 of support suggests the peak is set by the relative distance between two dense clusters. Whole-array phase shifts failed, but moving or stretching one cluster relative to the other changes the convolution plateau directly.
experiments.change: Split best at its largest zero gap (or at 0.5 if no gap). For delta in a schedule ±1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128 steps: copy best, shift the right part by delta (pad zeros, truncate if needed), then reoptimize all positive entries with _lbfgs_log and apply _window_polish_peak. Also try resampling the right part by stretch factors 0.98,0.99,1.01,1.02 using cumulative interpolation, then reoptimize. Accept the best; use remaining time alternating full and peak-window polish.
experiments.prediction: Aims for >=0.9410 on L1. A gain identifies the optimal inter-cluster spacing; unchanged means relative cluster placement is already locally optimal.

experiments.hypothesis: Random coarse multistart failed, but a weak deterministic periodic modulation of the current best can seed new support at specific spacings while retaining the good large-scale shape; local optimization can then grow beneficial spikes.

info.open_why: p0002 is the line's best and p0005 shows the only real gain path (multi-scale from trivial start), so I want their full code/results and F5's evidence to design experiments that either re-derive the good basin at higher N or exploit the 0.82 construction's structure.

plan.analysis: L1 is pinned at 0.940795: every local perturbation, support move, smoothing, phase shift and soft-max objective returned p0002 unchanged. The strongest untested lever is that p0002's resolution sweep was hard-truncated at 2x its starting N, so it stopped at 84992 without ever running at 130k+. I am betting on (i) a true resolution ladder beyond 2x, (ii) a symmetry-changing construction (mirror completion), which is a different basin because the ideal flat f*f is symmetric, and (iii) a direct flat-target objective that fits a rectangle of the same L1 instead of locally differentiating the ratio. These are larger changes than the failed perturbations and each tests a distinct structural assumption.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002's sweep only reached 2x its initial N (84992); finer steps may resolve narrower features and raise R, as the 42496->84992 step did.
experiments.change: Replace the fixed (N,1.5N,2N) sweep with an unbounded ladder from start: Nt in [130000,200000,300000,450000,650000,900000,1000000], stopping at deadline-5s. For each Nt: hp=_prolongate(best,Nt); hp=_rescale(hp); run _lbfgs_log(hp,300,deadline), then _window_polish_peak(hp,deadline,0.35,32), then another _lbfgs_log(hp,200,deadline). Keep best if R improves, but carry best forward even when a level does not improve. Print R at every Nt; use FFT convolution and leave 2s margin.
experiments.prediction: Target >0.9410 (ideally 0.9415). If R rises monotonically with N beyond 84992, resolution was limiting; if it stays 0.940795 at all N, the continuous basin is converged.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002 is asymmetric with the f*f peak at 0.296; the ideal flat f*f is symmetric, so mirror-completing f may enter a different, possibly better basin that local asymmetric perturbations cannot reach.
experiments.change: From start, form h0 = start + start[::-1] (N doubles to 169984), _rescale, and run the existing multi-scale pipeline: _lbfgs_log(h0,400,deadline); then _window_polish_peak at frac 0.10,0.20,0.35,0.50,0.75 with full _lbfgs_log after each; then repeat full+peak polish until deadline-2s. Also evaluate h0 before optimization and print its R. Keep the mirror-completed result even if it initially scores lower, and compare final R to 0.940795.
experiments.prediction: Target >0.9420. A gain means the asymmetric p0002 was a local trap and a symmetric basin exists; a large drop means symmetry is structurally worse for this ratio.

experiments.hypothesis: The ratio gradient only constrains argmax and L2, so it cannot easily fill valleys of f*f. Fitting an explicit flat rectangle with the same L1 targets the true equality case of Hoelder and may move off the p0002 plateau.
experiments.change: Coarse-grain start to Nc=4096. Compute L0=_knots(hc), M=max(L0), S0=sum(L0). Let plateau=[j: L0_j>=0.10*M], a=min(plateau), b=max(plateau), w=max(1,int(0.05*(b-a))). Build normalized shape q=1 on [a+w,b-w], linear ramps of width w to 0 at a and b, 0 elsewhere; set T=(S0/sum(q))*q. Minimize F(h)=sum_j (L_j-T_j)^2 + lambda*(sum(h)-sqrt(S0))^2 with h>=0 on the Nc grid via L-BFGS-B (additive bounds 0..inf), lambda=10*(M/sqrt(S0))^2, using the existing _backprop for the convolution adjoint. Run up to 500 iterations, _rescale, then prolongate 4096->8192->32768->84992, running _lbfgs_log and _window_polish_peak at each level; keep the best R. Print the final flatness residual sum(L-T)^2 and R.
experiments.prediction: Target >0.9415. If R rises while residual falls, direct flat-target fitting found a better basin; if residual falls but R does not, the rectangle is unattainable and the ratio plateau is intrinsic.

info.open_why: p0002 is the incumbent all experiments build on; F1 (support working-set) and F5 (the only gain) show which structural moves actually change this construction versus which are dead ends.

plan.analysis: Line L1 is stuck at 0.940795; every local perturbation (F9-F18, F6) returns the start unchanged, so the basin is exhausted. The gap to 1 is 5.9%, and R=1 requires f*f to be a flat rectangle. I bet on three global structural changes rather than more local polish: (1) Fourier phase retrieval that directly imposes a flat autoconvolution, (2) a low-dimensional superposition of inverse-square-root singularities, whose truncated autoconvolutions are flat plateaus, and (3) direct L2 gradient descent onto an explicit trapezoid target in the knot domain. Each is a different basin and each uses the whole 60 s.

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 is attained only when f*f is flat; local gradient methods cannot impose that global Fourier constraint. Alternating projections in Fourier between nonnegative f and a target flat autoconvolution can jump to a different basin that local polishing cannot reach.
experiments.change: Implement a Gerchberg-Saxton style construct: take start p0002, compute g=_knots(f) and M=max(g). Set support [a,b] where g>0.01*M, and build target Gt as a trapezoid of height M on [a,b] with ramp width 0.05*(b-a). Zero-pad f to length 2N. Iterate 3000 times: F=fft(f_pad); Ghat=fft(Gt_pad); Fnew=sqrt(abs(Ghat))*exp(1j*angle(F)); fnew=real(ifft(Fnew)); clip fnew to >=0; enforce support outside [a,b] to zero; rescale so sum(fnew)=sum(f). Every 100 iterations evaluate exact R on the current f and keep the best. Finally run the existing _lbfgs_log and peak polish on the best f. Use budget_seconds*0.95.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R>0.95 on L1. Result will show whether the Fourier-flat target produces a g with >60% of knots within 1% of max; if R stays <=0.940795 it shows the flat-rectangle target is unreachable from this basin by Fourier projection.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact convolution of two one-sided x^{-1/2} singularities is a flat plateau, so a small sum of truncated singularities can produce a much flatter f*f than the current spiky construction. This is a low-dimensional family that global optimisation can explore.
experiments.change: Ignore start. Build f on N=4000 steps as f_i = sum_{k=1..K} a_k / sqrt(max(eps, (i+0.5)/N - x_k)) for i/N > x_k and i/N <= L, else 0, with K=4, eps=1e-6, and parameters x_k in [0,L), a_k>0, L in (0,1]. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on parameters (x_k/L, log a_k, L) to maximise exact R, 2000 iterations, population 20. Take the best parameter set, prolongate to N=84992 by evaluating the same continuous formula on the finer grid, rescale, and run the existing _lbfgs_log plus peak-window polish until the deadline. Print the fitted parameters and final R.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R>0.95. The result will show whether a K=4 singularity superposition can beat 0.940795; if the best R is below 0.94, it indicates the singularity family is not competitive and the p0002 basin is close to the optimum for such shapes.

experiments.hypothesis: The ratio objective has a non-smooth max that stalls L-BFGS. Directly minimising ||f*f - trapezoid||^2 removes the max and explicitly fills valleys, which should flatten f*f and raise R.
experiments.change: From p0002, compute g=_knots(f), M=max(g), support [a,b] where g>0.02*M, ramp r=0.1*(b-a). Build target Gt: 0 outside [a,b], M on [a+r,b-r], linear ramps between. Define E=0.5*sum((g-Gt)^2). Implement analytic gradient: dE/dh = 2*correlate(g-Gt, h) (use fftconvolve with reversed h, mode 'valid', take first N). Minimise E over h>=0 with L-BFGS-B in log space (reuse _lbfgs_log structure but replace _fun_grad with this E and gradient). Every 100 iterations recompute a,b,r,M from the current g and rescale h so sum(h)=1. Run for the full budget, track best R via R_of, and finish with _lbfgs_log on R from the best h. Print E, R, and the fraction of knots within 1% of max.

plan.analysis: L2: 0.940795 has survived eight distinct perturbations (coarse-to-fine in both directions, soft-max, component relocation, unbounded resolution ladder) and F6 says the point is robust to every local move tried, so only a genuinely new basin or a curvature-based escape can help. Bets: (a) random coarse multistart + ladder to reach a different basin entirely; (b) a Lanczos negative-curvature escape — the one mechanism never tried at this plateau. L3: gains from finer N are shrinking (F29 +0.0058 at 32k, F30 +0.0020 at 205k), and its basin is smooth and low-contrast (max/mean 4.6, 0% zeros) while the 0.94 regime is spiky (97:1, 21% zeros, off-centre peak). Bet: a big move — replace L3's basin with sparse high-dynamic-range multistart ladders.

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.940795 point is a local optimum reached by descent from the warm start; random coarse starts refined upward can land in a different basin whose full-resolution polish exceeds it, since every perturbation of p0028 itself is absorbed by that basin (F6, F17, F25, F26, F27).
experiments.change: Ignore p0028's shape except as a fallback. At N0=512 draw 40 random starts: h=0 on a random 40-60% of entries, nonzero entries log-uniform in [1e3,1e-3] times a random envelope, then keep() only starts with R>0.4. Polish each at N0 with _lbfgs_log(800 iters) and take the top 5. For each of the top 5, run a doubling ladder N0->1024->2048->...->32768->42496 using _prolongate, at each level _lbfgs_log(500 iters) followed by _window_polish_peak(frac 0.25, extra 16); after every level record R_of. Spend remaining time (up to deadline-1s) doing _lbfgs_log + peak-polish on the best ladder result, then return the better of that and the rescaled start p0028.
experiments.prediction: Aim: >0.9410 (i.e. a genuine new basin). Diagnostic: if any ladder reaches R>0.93 at 8192 steps but collapses back to 0.940795 at 42496, the basin is unique and strong; if nothing exceeds 0.90 at any level, random sparse starts cannot reach the high-contrast regime at these sizes.

experiments.hypothesis: The plateau is likely a constrained local max with many near-max knots (42.8% within 5% of max); if it is only a saddle or a flat valley, the negative-curvature direction of the reduced Hessian over the nonzero coordinates will lead to a better point, and no experiment has yet used curvature information.
experiments.change: Take p0028, active = indices with h>1e-8*max(h), define g(u) = gradient of -log R w.r.t. active heights (reuse _fun_grad, return g[active]). Run 30-step Lanczos (or power iteration on c*I-H with c=1.5*max|diag|) applying Hv = (g(h+eps*v)-g(h-eps*v))/(2*eps) with eps = 1e-6*max(h)*sqrt(n_active)/||v||_2, clipping h+-eps*v at 0, to get the most negative eigenvalue lambda_min and vector v. If lambda_min<0: for alpha in {0.5,1,2,4}*alpha0 with alpha0 = 0.01*max(h)/max|v|, set h' = clip(h+alpha*v,0), rescale, run full _lbfgs_log(1500 iters) + _window_polish_peak(0.3,16), keep if R improves; loop up to 8 escapes inside the budget. If lambda_min>=0 (positive definite), do the same along the *flattest* eigenvector and record it, then finish with a full _lbfgs_log polish and return the best of all candidates and the start.
experiments.prediction: Aim: 0.9415+. Diagnostic to report: lambda_min of the reduced Hessian at p0028 (a small negative value means the plateau is escapable by curvature; lambda_min>=0 with all escapes returning to 0.940795 proves the point is a genuine second-order local max).

plan.analysis: L2 (0.940795) has survived every local and soft-max escape tried (F31–F40): the plateau is structural at fixed knot geometry, and the 0.94 regime is spiky (97:1, 21% zeros). The untested lever is the knot geometry itself — moving/splitting the spikes of the incumbent at coarse resolution rather than reweighting fixed steps; that is what I bet on there. L3 (0.826931) is a smooth local basin that keeps paying a little for resolution (F41) and keeps rejecting from-scratch sparse starts (F32/F35/F42) because L-BFGS refills zeros. Two distinct bets: (a) forbid refilling by optimising on a *constrained* zero mask and unfreezing progressively; (b) directly flatten the top of f*f with a fixed-beta logsumexp surrogate (never tried on L3, whose peak is rounded and responsive, unlike L2's kink).

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.940795 ceiling is a limit of the incumbent's *knot positions*, not of its heights: every height-only or soft-max move returns it unchanged. Re-optimising the spike geometry (integer moves/merges of a coarse spike train) changes the combinatorial arrangement that sets the flat top of f*f, which is exactly what the ratio rewards.
experiments.change: Coarsen p0028 to Nc=2048 (mass-conserving sum of blocks) and extract its spikes as a list of (index, height) with K<=300 entries (threshold 1e-4*max, each run of nonzero steps -> one spike with its summed mass on the run's centre index). Then run coordinate descent on the *geometry* at Nc: loop over spikes in random order, for each try shifting its index by ±1,±2,±3,±5 (merge mass if it lands on an existing spike, drop if it leaves [0,Nc-1]) and accept if R at Nc increases by >1e-12; after each full sweep re-optimise the spike heights with _lbfgs_block(maxiter=300) on the nonzero indices only. Do ~60 sweeps or until 25 s used. Then take the best coarse spike train, _prolongate to 42496, _rescale, and run _lbfgs_log(800) + _window_polish_peak(frac=0.15, extra=16) + _lbfgs_log(800) alternating until the deadline. Return the better of that and the rescaled start (compare R_of). Use the full budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.9415 on L2 (clearly above the 0.940795 plateau). Diagnostic: if R at Nc=2048 of the moved spike train exceeds R of the plain coarsened p0028 by >= 2e-3 at the same Nc, geometry is the binding constraint; the returned shape should show max/mean > 120 and a larger zero fraction (>25%) than p0028's 20.9%. If no coarse geometric move is accepted at all, the plateau is structural in the spike arrangement and the returned array will be the start.

experiments.hypothesis: Sparse starts collapse back into the smooth 0.827 basin only because L-BFGS is free to refill zeros (F35, F42). If the zero set is a hard constraint during optimisation and only released progressively, the optimiser is forced to reach a high-dynamic-range shape at low N, which can then be grown.
experiments.change: Coarsen p0050 to N0=16384 (mass-conserving cumulative interpolation). Build a mask: pick contiguous blocks of width w~U{1,64} covering ~35% of the steps and set them to zero (preferentially at the lowest |h| positions, keep step 0 and N0-1 nonzero). Freeze those entries to zero and optimise only the free entries with _lbfgs_block(maxiter=400, deadline). Then run 6 unfreeze rounds: each round release one third of the still-frozen entries that are adjacent to a nonzero entry (ties by larger neighbouring mass), re-optimise the free set, and record R; total ~8 optimisations at N0 = 16384. Keep two branches alive (the best R and the spikiest by max/mean) and ladder only the better one: _prolongate to 65536, _rescale, _lbfgs_log(600) + _window_polish_peak(0.10, 8); then to 131072 and 262144 if >= 15 s remain, each with _lbfgs_log(600) + _window_polish_peak(0.05,4) + _window_polish_peak(0.10,8). Spend the remaining time alternating _lbfgs_log(800) and _window_polish_peak(0.10,8) on the best, and return the better of that and the rescaled start.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.840 on L3. Diagnostic: after the final unfreeze round at N0, zeros fraction still >= 15% and max/mean >= 8 means a genuinely different basin was reached and the ladder should carry it past 0.83; if zeros fill back in and R at N0 sits at ~0.827, the smooth basin survives even hard support constraints and the returned shape will again be max/mean ~4.5 with the peak near 0.55 of the support.

experiments.hypothesis: The L3 solution's f*f top is much narrower than L2's (19.6% of knots within 1% of max vs 33.9%), so R is still limited by peak sharpness. A logsumexp surrogate with a moderate *fixed* beta pushes all near-max knots toward equality (widening the flat top) instead of chasing the single argmax; on L3's smooth rounded peak this surrogate is well-conditioned, unlike the kinked L2 case where it failed.
experiments.change: Add _fun_grad_sm(h, beta): build Lf=_knots(h); with M=Lf.max() and w=exp(beta*(Lf-M)); S=w.sum(); Lm_s = M + log(S)/beta; num as usual; gLf = -dq/num with gLf[m] replaced by the soft weights gLf += beta*w/S (i.e. d(log Lm_s)/dLf_j = w_j/S ... implement as gLf += w/S, the derivative of log Lm_s times ... note: d Lm_s/dLf_j = w_j/S). L-BFGS in log-heights with the same jac wrapper as _lbfgs_log. Run at N=32768 (coarsened p0050): for beta in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64} (L normalised to unit max) run _lbfgs_sm up to 300 iterations, then a true-objective _lbfgs_log(400) + _window_polish_peak(0.10,8), keeping the true-objective best. If a true-objective improvement over the start appears at 32768, ladder it 65536 -> 131072 -> 262144 with a shortened homotopy (beta in {16,64}) plus true-objective polish at each level; otherwise spend the remaining budget on the true-objective polish loop (_lbfgs_log + _window_polish_peak(0.10,8) alternations) on the incumbent. Return the best, never worse than the rescaled start.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.838 on L3. Diagnostic: the share of f*f knots within 1% of the maximum should rise from 19.6% to >= 25% while max/mean stays near 4-6; if the 1%-share does not move (stays ~19.6%) the peak is already as flat as this construction allows and the surrogate is inert, which the result will show as R within 1e-6 of 0.826931.
